questions.q: $Let $f\left(x\right) = \left(sin\left(\tan^{- 1}x\right) + sin\left(\cot^{- 1}x\right)\right)2 - 1$,~\left|x\right| > 1$. If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d}{dx}  \left(\sin^{- 1} \left($f \left(x\right)\right)\right)$ and~$y \$left(\sqrt{3}\right) = \dfrac{π}{6},then y \left(- \sqrt{3}\right)is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $\tan^{- 1}x = \theta$

$⇒ x = tan\theta ⇒ sin\theta = \dfrac{x}{1 + x^{2}}$

So,~$y = \left(\dfrac{x}{1 + x^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}\right)2 - 1$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{ \left(x + 1\right)2}{1 + x^{2}} - 1$

$⇒ y = $\dfrac{2x}{1 + x^{2}} ==$f\left($x\right)$

Now,~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{1}{1 - f^{2}} \timesf^{'} \left(x\right)$

$= $\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{4x^{2}}{ \left(1 + x^{2}\right)2}}$f \left($x\right)$

$= \left($1 + x^{2}\right)2 \left(x^{2} - 1\right)f^{'}\left(x\right)$

$= \dfrac{1 + x^{2}}{2\left(x^{2} - 1\right)} \ttimes2\dfrac{1 + x^{2} - 2x^{2}}{\left(1 + x^{2}\right)2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{\left(x^{2} - 1\right)\left(1 + x^{2}\right)}

$⇒ dy = $\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{\left(x^{2} - 1\right)\left(1 + x^{2}\right)}$dx$

Integrating both sides with respect to~$x$

$∫ dy = ∫ $\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{\left(x^{2} - 1\right)\left(1 + x^{2}\right)}$dx$

$⇒ y = - \tan^{- 1}x + c$

Given,~y\left(\sqrt{3}\right) = \dfrac{π}{6}$⇒ $\dfrac{π}{6} = - \dfrac{π}{3} +$c ⇒ c = $\dfrac{π}{2}

$y = - \tan^{- 1}x + $\dfrac{π}{2} = \cot^{- 1}$x$

Now,~y\left(- \sqrt{3}\right) = \cot^{- 1$1$1$1}x\left(- $\sqrt{3}$\right) = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$

questions.q: $If $y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x \left[\dfrac{y2}{x2} + \dfrac{ϕ \left(\dfrac{y2}{x2}\right)}${{ϕ}^{'} \$left(\dfrac{y2}{x2}\right)}\right],x > 0, ϕ > 0,$~and $y ( 1 ) = - 1,$~then $ϕ  \left(\dfrac{y2}{4}\right)$is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given:$\dfrac{y}{x}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left[\dfrac{y2}{x2} + \dfrac{ϕ \left(\dfrac{y2}{x2}\right)}${{ϕ}^{'}$\$left(\dfrac{y2}{x2}\right)}\right] . . . . \left($1\right)$~

Let~$\dfrac{y}{x} =t$

$⇒ y = xt$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} =t + x $\cdot $\dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$∴ t\left($t + x\dfrac{dt}{dx}\right) = \left(t^{2} + \dfrac{ϕ \left($t^{2}\right)}${{ϕ}^{'}\left($t^{2}\right)}\right)

$⇒ $xt\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{ϕ\left(t^{2}\right)}{ϕ ' \left(t^{2}\right)}

$⇒ $\dfrac{t \cdot {ϕ}^{'}\left(t^{2}\right)}{ϕ\left(t^{2}\right)}$dt = $\dfrac{1}{x}$dx$
Integrating both sides

$∫ $\dfrac{t \cdot {ϕ}^{'}\left(t^{2}\right)}{ϕ\left(t^{2}\right)}$dt = ∫ $\dfrac{1}{x}$dx$

Let~$ϕ\left(t^{2}\right) = p$

$⇒ {ϕ}^{'}\left(t^{2}\right) . 2t = dp$

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{2}$∫ $\dfrac{1}{p}$dp = ∫ $\dfrac{1}{x}$dx$

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{2}$lnp = lnx + C$

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{2}$lnϕ\left(t^{2}\right) = lnx + C$

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{2}$ln \left(ϕ \left(\dfrac{y2}{x2}\right)\right) =$lnx + C . . . \left($2\right)$

If~$x = 1, y = - 1$~then~$C = $\dfrac{1}{2}$ln \left($ϕ \left(1\right)\right)$

Substituting value of~$C$~in~ \left(2\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{2}ln \left(ϕ \left(\dfrac{y2}{x2}\right)\right) =$lnx + $\d$dfrac{1}{2}ln\left($ϕ\left($1\right)\right)$

$⇒ln \left($ϕ \left(\dfrac{y2}{x2}\right)\right) =lnx^{2} + ln\left(ϕ\left(1\right)\right)$

If~$x = 2$~then~

$ln \left(ϕ \left(\dfrac{y2}{4}\right)\right) =$ln4 + $ln\left($ϕ\left($1\right)\right)$

SO,~$ϕ \left(\dfrac{y2}{4}\right) =$4ϕ \left(1\right)$

$

questions.q: Let a curve $y=f(x)$ pass through the points $(0,5)$ and  \left(\log _e 2, k\right)$. If the curve satisfies the differential equation $2(3+y) e^{2 x} d x-\left(7+e^{2 x}\right) d y=0$, then $k$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{2(3+y) \cdot e^{2 x}}{7+e^{2 x}} \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{2 y e^{2 x}}{7+e^{2 x}}=\frac{6 \cdot e^{2 x}}{7+e^{2 x}} \\ & \text { I.F. }=e^{-\int \frac{2 e^{2 x}}{7+e^{2 x}} d x} \\ & \Rightarrow e^{-\ln \left(7+e^{2 x}\right)} \\ & =\frac{1}{7+e^{2 x}} \\ & y \cdot \frac{1}{7+e^{2 x}}=\int \frac{6 e^{2 x}}{\left(7+e^{2 x}\right)^2} d x \\ & \frac{y}{7+e^{2 x}}=\frac{-3}{7+e^{2 x}+C} \\ & \therefore y(0)=5 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{5}{8}=\frac{-3}{8}+C \\ & \Rightarrow C=1 \\ & \therefore y=-3+7+e^{2 x} \\ & y=e^{2 x}+4 \\ & \therefore k=8\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The surface area of a balloon of spherical shape being inflated, increases at a constant rate. If initially, the radius of balloon is& $3$ units and after $5$~seconds, it becomes~$7$ units, then its radius after~$9$ seconds is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let surface area of the spherical balloon& $A = 4\pir^{2}$

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 8\pir\dfrac{dr}{dt} = k$~(let)~$. . . \left(1\right)$

On integrating on both sides w.r.t~$t$ , we get

$4\pir^{2} = kt + C$~.~

Given that, at $t = 0, r = 3$.

$⇒ 36\pi =C$

Also~given that, at $t = 5, r = 7$

$⇒ 4\pi \times49 = 5k + 36\pi$

$⇒ 5k = 4\pi \left(49 - 9\right)$~ ~$⇒ 5k = 4\pi \times 40$~

$⇒ k = 32\pi$

On substituting~$k$~value in equation~ \left(1\right)$we get,~$4\pir^{2} = 32\pit + 36\pi$

$⇒ r^{2} = 8t + 9$

Given~$t = 9$.

$⇒ r^{2} = 81 ⇒ r = 9$.

$

questions.q: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation \left(1+y^2\right) e^{\tan x} d x+\cos ^2 x \left($1+e^{2 \tan x}\right) d y=0, y(0)=1$. Then y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)is equal to

questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \left(1+y^2\right) e^{\tan x} d x+\cos ^2 x\left(1+e^{2 \tan x}\right) d y=0 \\ & \int \frac{\sec ^2 x e^{\tan x}}{1+e^{2 \tan x}} d x+\int \frac{d y}{1+y^2}=C \\ & \Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}\left(e^{\tan x}\right)+\tan ^{-1} y=C \\ & \text { for } x=0, y=1, \tan ^{-1}(1)+\tan ^{-1} 1=C\end{aligned}\mathrm{C}=\frac{\pi}{2}\tan ^{-1}\left(e^{\tan x}\right)+\tan ^{-1} y=\frac{\pi}{2}$

questions.q: $Let& $x = x  \left(y\right)$~be the solution of the differential equation~$2\left(y + 2\$right)\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left($y + 2\right)dx + \left($x + 4 - 2\log_{\mathrm{e}}  \left($y + 2\right)\right)dy = 0$,~$y > - 1$~with~x\left($e^{4} - 2\right) = 1$. Then~x\left($e^{9} - 2\right)$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$2\left(y + 2\right)\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(y + 2\right)dx + \left(x + 4 - 2\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(y + 2\right)\right)dy = 0$

Let~$x + 4 = u, y + 2 = v$

$dx = du, dy = dv$

So, the equation becomes,

\left(2vlnv\right)du = - \left(u - 2lnv\right)dv$

$⇒ 2vlnv\dfrac{du}{dv} + u = 2lnv$

$⇒ \dfrac{du}{dv} + \dfrac{1}{2vlnv} . u = \dfrac{1}{v}$

Which is a linear differential equation,

So,~$IF = e^{\dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{1}{vlnv}} = e^{\dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(lnv\right)} = \left(lnv\right)\dfrac{1}{2}$

Now solution of differential equation is given by,

$u \cdot \left(lnv\right)\dfrac{1}{2} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{v} \cdot \left(lnv\right)\dfrac{1}{2}dv$

$⇒ u \cdot \left(lnv\right)\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{2}{3}\left($lnv\$right)\dfrac{3}{2} +$c . . . . . . . \left($i\right)$

Now using given value,~$y = e^{4} - 2 ⇒ x = 1$

$∴ v = e^{4} ⇒ u = 5$

$5 $\cdot \$left(4\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{2}{3} \cdot \left($4\right)\dfrac{3}{2} +c$

$⇒ 10 = \dfrac{16}{3} +c$

$⇒ c = \dfrac{14}{3}$

Now finding,~$y = e^{9} - 2 ⇒ v = y + 2 = e^{9}$

Now putting the value in equation~ \left($i\right)$~we get,

$⇒ u $\cdot$3 = $\dfrac{2}{3} \times$27 + $\dfrac{14}{3} =$18 + $\dfrac{14}{3}

$⇒ x + 4 = u = 6 + $\dfrac{14}{9}

$⇒ x = 2 + $\dfrac{14}{9} = \dfrac{32}{9}

questions.q: Let the solution curve of the differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = \sqrt{y^{2} + 16x^{2}}, y  \left(1\right) = 3$~be $y = y\left(x\right)$. Then $y  \left(2\right)$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$x\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = \sqrt{y^{2} + 16x^{2}}$~

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sqrt{y^{2} + 16x^{2}} + y}{x}$

Let~$y = xt ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = x\dfrac{dt}{dx} + t$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dt}{dx} + t = t + \sqrt{t^{2} + 16}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{t^{2} + 16} = \dfrac{dx}{x}$

Now integrating both side we get,

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dt}{t^{2} + 16} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ ln\left|t + \sqrt{t^{2} + 16}\right| = lnx + lnc$

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{x} + \dfrac{y^{2} + 16x^{2}}{x} = cx$

$∵ y\left(1\right) = 3$~so~$⇒ \dfrac{3}{1} + \dfrac{{3}^{2} + 16 \times {1}^{2}}{1} = c \times 1 ⇒ c = 8$

So solution becomes,

$\dfrac{y}{x} + \dfrac{y^{2} + 16x^{2}}{x} = 8x$

Now~$y\left(2\right) = \dfrac{y}{2} + \dfrac{y^{2} + 16 \times {2}^{2}}{2} = 8 \times 2$

$⇒ y + \sqrt{y^{2} + 64} = 32$

$⇒ y = 15$

questions.q:
Let $f:[0, \infty) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable function such that $f(\mathrm{x})=1-2 \mathrm{x}+\int_0^x e^{x-t} f(t) \mathrm{dt}$ for all $\mathrm{x} \in[0, \infty)$.
Then the area of the region bounded by $\mathrm{y}=f(\mathrm{x})$ and the coordinate axes is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & y=1-2 x+e^x \int_0^x e^{-t} f(t) d t \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}=-2+e^{-x} \cdot e^x f(x)+e^x \int_0^x e^{-t} f(t) d t \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}=-2+y+y+2 x-1 \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}-2 y=(2 x-3) \\ & y e^{-2 x}=\int(2 x-3) d x \cdot e^{-2 x} \\ & y e^{-2 x}=\frac{-(2 x-3)}{2} e^{-2 x}+\int e^{-2 x} d x \\ & y e^{-2 x}=\frac{-(2 x-3)}{2} e^{-2 x}-\frac{1}{2} e^{-2 x}+c \\ & f(0)=1 \Rightarrow c=1-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{2}=0\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & y=-\frac{(2 x-3)}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\ & y=-x+1 \\ & x+y=1 \\ & \text { area }=\frac{1}{2}(1)(1)=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the solution $y=y(x)$ of the differential equation \left(x^4+2 x^3+3 x^2+2 x+2\right) \mathrm{d} y-\left(2 x^2+2 x+3\right) \mathrm{d} x=0$ satisfies $y(-1)=-\frac{\pi}{4}$, then $y(0)$ is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int d y=\int \frac{\left(2 x^2+2 x+3\right)}{x^4+2 x^3+3 x^2+2 x+2} d x \\ & y=\int \frac{\left(2 x^2+2 x+3\right)}{\left(x^2+1\right)\left(x^2+2 x+2\right)} d x \\ & y=\int \frac{d x}{x^2+2 x+2}+\int \frac{d x}{x^2+1} \\ & y=\tan ^{-1}(x+1)+\tan ^{-1} x+C \\ & y(-1)=\frac{-\pi}{4} \\ & \frac{-\pi}{4}=0-\frac{\pi}{4}+C \Rightarrow C=0 \\ & \Rightarrow y=\tan ^{-1}(x+1)+\tan ^{-1} x \\ & y(0)=\tan ^{-1} 1=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}$

If both the curves pass through \left(1, 1\right),$ then the area (in sq. units) enclosed by the curves ${C}_{1}$~and ${C}_{2}$ is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^{2} - x^{2}}{2xy}, x \in \left($0, $\infty\right)

put $y = vx$

$x$\dfrac{dv}{dx} +$v = $\dfrac{v^{2} - 1}{2v}

\dfrac{2v}{v^{2} + 1}$dv = - $\dfrac{dx}{x}

Integrate,
$ln\left($v^{2} + 1\right) = - lnx + C$

$ln\left(\dfrac{y2}{x2} +$1\right) = - lnx + C$

put $x = 1, y = 1, C = ln2$

$ln\left(\dfrac{y2}{x2} +$1\right) = - lnx + ln2$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x = 0$ (Curve~${C}_{1}$)

Similarly,

\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2xy}{x^{2} - y^{2}}

Put $y = vx$

$x^{2} + y^{2} - 2y = 0$

Required area $= 2{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\sqrt{2x - x^{2}} -$x\right)dx = $\dfrac{π}{2} -$1$ \text{ and } sq. units

$

questions.q: The solution of the differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2y = x^{2}, ( x \ne 0 )$ with $y\left(1\right) = 1$, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, differential equation is& $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)y = x$

This is a linear differential equation of type~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$~where~$P \text{ and } Q$~are the functions of~$x$~or constants.

Thus,~$P = \dfrac{2}{x} \text{ and } Q = x$

The integrating factor~$I . F . = e^{∫ Pdx}$

$= e^{∫ \dfrac{2}{x}dx} = e^{2lnx}$

$= e^{lnx^{2}} = x^{2} .$

The solution of the linear differential equation is~$y \times \left(I . F .\right) = ∫ \left(Q \times I . F .\right)dx + C$~

So, the solution of the~given differential equation is

$yx^{2} = ∫ x \cdot x^{2}dx + C$

$⇒ x^{2}y = ∫ x^{3}dx + C$

Using~$∫ x^{n}dx = \dfrac{xn + 1}{n + 1},$~we get

$⇒ x^{2}y = \dfrac{x4}{4} + C$

Since $y\left(1\right) = 1$

$⇒ 1 \cdot 1 = \dfrac{1}{4} + C$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ x^{2}y = \dfrac{x4}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{x2}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4x^{2}} .$

questions.q:
Let $y = y \left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation e^{x}\sqrt{1 - y^{2}}$dx + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)dy = 0, y\left(1\right) = - 1$
Then the value of \l$left(y\left($3\right)\right)2$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$e^{x}\sqrt{1 - y^{2}}dx + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)dy = 0, y\left(1\right) = - 1$

$⇒ e^{x}\sqrt{1 - y^{2}}dx = \left(\dfrac{- y}{x}\right)dy$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{- y}{1 - y^{2}}dy = ∫ xe^{x}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{d\left(1 - y^{2}\right)}{1 - y^{2}}dy = ∫ xe^{x}dx$

$⇒ \sqrt{1 - y^{2}} = e^{x}\left(x - 1\right) + c$

Now, at~$x = 1, y = - 1$, then

$⇒ 0 = 0 + c ⇒ c = 0$

$∴ \sqrt{1 - y^{2}} = e^{x} \left(x - 1\right)$

At $x = 3$, then

\sqrt{1 - \left(y\left(3\right)\right)2} =$2e^{3}$

$⇒ 1 - $\l$left(y\left($3\right)\right)2 = 4e^{6}$

$⇒ $\lleft(y\left(3\right)\right)2 = 1 - 4e^{6}

$

questions.q:
If the solution curve $f ( x, y ) = 0$~of the differential equation \left(1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right)\dfrac{dx}{dy} - x\log_{\mathrm{e}}x = e^{y}, x > 0,$~passes through the points $( 1, 0 )$~and $( a, 2 )$, then $a^{a}$ \text{ and } is equal to

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is

\left(1 + ln\left(x\right)\right)\dfrac{dx}{dy} - xln\left(x\right) = e^{y}$

Put~$xln\left(x\right) = t$

$⇒ \left(1 + ln\left(x\right)\right)dx = dt$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dy} - t = e^{y}$~which is a linear differential equation.

$I . F = e^{- ∫ dy}$

$= e^{- y}$

The solution of the differential equation is

$⇒ t \times e^{- y} = ∫ e^{y} \times e^{- y}dy + c$

$⇒ t \times e^{- y} = y + c$

$⇒ xln\left(x\right) = ye^{y} + ce^{y}$

Put~$x = 1, y = 0$

$⇒ c = 0$

Put~$x = a, y = 2$

$aln\left(a\right) = 2e^{2}$

$∴ a^{a} = e^{2e^{2}}$

Hence this is the correct option.

$

questions.q: $If& $y = y  \left(x\right)$~is the solution of the differential equation~ \left($1 + e^{2x}\$right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} +$+2\left($1 + y^{2}\right)e^{x} = 0$~and~$y \left($0\right) = 0$, then~6 \left($y ' \left($0\right) + $\lleft(y\left(\log_{\mathrm{c}}\sqrt{3}\right)\right)2\right)$& is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given,

\left(1 + e^{2x}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2\left(1 + y^{2}\right)e^{x} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{1 + y^{2}} + \dfrac{2e^{x}}{1 + e^{2x}}dx = 0$~.........(i)

Now~integrating both side we get,

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dy}{1 + y^{2}} + ∫ \dfrac{2e^{x}}{1 + e^{2x}}dx = ∫ 0$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}y + 2\tan^{- 1}e^{x} = c$

$∵ y\left(0\right) = 0$

so,~$C = \dfrac{π}{2} ⇒ \tan^{- 1}y + 2\tan^{- 1}e^{x} = \dfrac{π}{2}$~....(ii)

Now from equation~(i), we get~\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)x = 0 = - 1$

From equation (ii)~we get,~$y$~(In~$\sqrt{3} ) = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

So,~$6 \left[y ' \left($0\right) + ( y\right$~In~\$left\sqrt{3}{)}^{2}\right] ==$6\left[-1 + $\dfrac{1}{3}\right] = -$4$.

$

questions.q: Let $g$ be a differentiable function such that $\int_0^x g(t) d t=x-\int_0^x \operatorname{tg}(t) d t, x \geq 0$ and let $y=y(x)$ satisfy the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}-y \tan x=2(x+1) \sec x g(x), x \in  \left[$0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right).$If $y(0)=0$, then $y \left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Diff. w.r.t. x
$\begin{aligned}
& g(x)=1-x g(x) \\ & g(x)=\frac{1}{1+x} \\ & \text { so } \frac{d y}{d x}-y \tan x=2 \sec x \\ & I F=e^{-\int \tan d x}=e^{\log \cos x}=\cos x
\end{aligned}$
solution of D.E.
$\begin{aligned}
& y \cos x=\int 2 d x+c \\ & y \cos x=2 x+c \\ & y(0)=0
\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{c}=0$
$\begin{aligned} & y=\frac{2 x}{\cos x} \\ & y=2 x \sec x \\ & y\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=2 \cdot \frac{\pi}{3} \cdot 2=\frac{4 \pi}{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{2}^{x}y + {2}^{y} \cdot {2}^{x}}{{2}^{x} + {2}^{x + y}\log_{\mathrm{e}}2}, y\left(0\right) = 0,$~then for $y = 1,$~the value of $x$ lies in the interval :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{2}^{x} \cdot y + {2}^{y} \cdot {2}^{x}}{{2}^{x} + {2}^{x + y}\log_{\mathrm{e}}2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{2}^{x}\left(y + {2}^{y}\right)}{{2}^{x}\left(1 + {2}^{y}\log_{\mathrm{e}}2\right)}$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{1 + {2}^{y}\log_{\mathrm{e}}2}{y + {2}^{y}}dy = ∫ dx$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{d\left(y + {2}^{y}\right)}{y + {2}^{y}} = ∫ dx$

$⇒ ln\left|y + {2}^{y}\right| = x + C \left[∵ ∫ $\dfrac{f^{'} \left(x\right)}{f \left(x\right)}$dx = $ln\lleft(f\left(x\right)\right) + C\right]$

Now $∵ y\left(0\right) = 0$

$⇒ C = 0$

$∴ ln\left|y + {2}^{y}\right| = x$

Now for $y = 1$~we have

$x = ln \left(1 + 2\right) = ln3 \in \left(1, 2\right)$

$

questions.q: $If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{3}{\cos^{2}x}y = \dfrac{1}{\cos^{2}x}$ , $x \in \left(- \dfrac{π}{3}, \dfrac{π}{3}\right),$ and $y \$left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{4}{3},$then y \left(- \dfrac{π}{4}\right)equals
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(3\sec^{2}x\right)y = \sec^{2}x$

This is linear differential equation, of the type~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$~where~$P \text{ and } Q$~are functions of~$x$~or constants.

Here,~$P = 3sec^{2}x \text{ and } Q = sec^{2}x$

Now, integrating factor $I . F . = e^{∫ Pdx}$

$= e^{∫ 3\sec^{2}xdx} = e^{3tanx}$

Hence, the solution of the differential equation is~$y\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q\left(I . F .\right)dx + c$

$⇒ y \cdot e^{3tanx} = ∫ e^{3tanx} \cdot \sec^{2}xdx$

Let,~$tanx = t, ⇒ sec^{2}xdx = dt$

$⇒ y \cdot e^{3tanx} = ∫ e^{3t}dt + c$

$⇒ y \cdot e^{3tanx} = \dfrac{e3t}{3} + c$

$⇒ y \cdot e^{3tanx} = \dfrac{e3tanx}{3} + c$

$⇒ y = ce^{- 3tanx} + \dfrac{1}{3}$

Given,~$y\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{4}{3} ⇒$

$\dfrac{4}{3} = ce^{- 3} + \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ c = e^{3}$

Thus,~$y = e^{3} \cdot e^{- 3tanx} + \dfrac{1}{3}$

Hence,~$y\left(- \dfrac{π}{4}\right) = e^{3} \cdot e^{- 3\left(tan\left(- \dfrac{π}{4}\right)\right)} + \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ y\left(- \dfrac{π}{4}\right) = e^{3} \cdot e^{- 3\left(- 1\right)} + \dfrac{1}{3}$

$= e^{3} \cdot e^{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} = e^{6} + \dfrac{1}{3} .$

questions.q: Let& $y = y  \left(x\right)$~be the solution of the differential equation,~\dfrac{2 + sinx}{y + 1} . \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -$cosx$,~$y > 0, y\left(0\right) = 1$.~If~$y  \left(\pi\right) =a$~and~$\dfrac{dy}{dx}$~at~$x = \pi$~is~$b$, then the ordered pair~\left(a, b\right)$ \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{1 + y} = \dfrac{- cosx}{2 + sinx}dx$

ln\left($1 + y\right) = - ln\left($2 + sinx\right) + lnc

\left(1 + y\right)\left(2 + sinx\right) = c$

We know~$y\left(0\right) = 1$

So
c = 4

1 + y = $\dfrac{4}{2 + sinx}$⇒ y = $\dfrac{4}{2 + sinx} -$1

$y\left(\pi\right) = 2 - 1 = 1 = a$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{- 4}{ \left($2 + sinx\right)2} $\cdot$cosx = 1$

At~$x = $\pi$⇒ b = 1$

\left(a, b\right) = \left(1, 1\right)$

$

questions.q: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation \left(x^2+4\right)^2 d y+\left(2 x^3 y+8 x y-2\right) d x=0$. If $y(0)=0$, then $y(2)$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{d y}{d x}+y\left(\frac{2 x^3+8 x}{\left(x^2+4\right)^2}\right)=\frac{2}{\left(x^2+4\right)^2} \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}+y\left(\frac{2 x}{x^2+4}\right)=\frac{2}{\left(x^2+4\right)^2} \\
& \text { IF }=e^{\int \frac{2 x}{x^2+4} d x} \\
& \text { IF }=x^2+4 \\
& y \times\left(x^2+4\right)=\int \frac{2}{\left(x^2+4\right)^2} \times\left(x^2+4\right) \\
& y\left(x^2+4\right)=2 \int \frac{d x}{x^2+2^2} \\
& y\left(x^2+4\right)=\frac{2}{2} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+c \\
& 0=0+c=c=0 \\
& y\left(x^2+4\right)=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) \\
& y \text { at } x=2 \\
& y(4+4)=\tan ^{-1}(1) \\
& y(2)=\frac{\pi}{32}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation \left(1 - x^{2}\right)dy = \left[xy + \left(x^{3} + 2\right)\sqrt{3\left(1 - x^{2}\right)}\right]dx$, $- 1 < x < 1, y ( 0 ) = 0$. If $y\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{m}{n}, m$ and $n$ are coprime numbers, then $m + n$ is equal to __________.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left(1 - x^{2}\right)dy = \left[xy + \left(x^{3} + 2\right)\sqrt{3\left(1 - x^{2}\right)}\right]dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{xy}{1 - x^{2}} = \dfrac{\left(x^{3} + 2\right)\sqrt{3\left(1 - x^{2}\right)}}{1 - x^{2}}$

The above equation is a linear differential equation,

So, $IF = e^{- ∫ \dfrac{x}{1 - x^{2}}dx} = e^{\dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(1 - x^{2}\right)} = \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}$

Now, the solution of the differential equation is given by,

$y\sqrt{1 - x^{2}} = ∫ \dfrac{\left(x^{3} + 2\right)\sqrt{3\left(1 - x^{2}\right)}}{1 - x^{2}} \times \sqrt{\left(1 - x^{2}\right)}dx$

$⇒ y\sqrt{1 - x^{2}} = \sqrt{3} ∫ \left(x^{3} + 2\right)dx$

$⇒ y\sqrt{1 - x^{2}} = \sqrt{3}\left(\dfrac{x4}{4} + 2x\right) + c$

Now, using $y ( 0 ) = 0$ we get, $c = 0$

Now, finding $y \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)

y\sqrt{1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$2$2$2}=\sqrt{3} $\$left(\dfrac{1}{{2}^{4} \cdot 4} +2 $\cdot $\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$⇒ y = $\$left(\dfrac{1}{32} +$2\right)$

$⇒ y\$left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{65}{32} = \dfrac{m}{n}

Hence, $m + n = 97$

$

questions.q: Let $S = \left(0, 2\pi\right) -  \left\{\dfrac{π}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right$\}. Let $y = $y  \left(x\right)$, $x \in S$, be the solution curve of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{1 + sin2x},y\$left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}.If the sum of abscissas of all the points of intersection of the curve $y = y  \left(x\right)$~with the curve $y = \sqrt{2}sinx$~is $\dfrac{k\pi}{12},$then $k$& is equal to _____.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given differential equation& $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{1 + sin2x}$

$∫ dy = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{\left(sinx + cosx\right)2}$

$∫ dy = ∫ \dfrac{\sec^{2}x}{\left(1 + tanx\right)2}$

$y = - \dfrac{1}{1 + tanx} + C$

So~$y\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

So~$\dfrac{1}{2} = - \dfrac{1}{2} + C⇒ C = 1$

So~$y = \dfrac{- 1}{1 + tanx} + 1$

$y = \dfrac{- 1 + 1 + tanx}{1 + tanx}$

$y = \dfrac{tanx}{1 + tanx}$

Solving this equation with~$y = \sqrt{2}sinx$

$\dfrac{tanx}{1 + tanx} = \sqrt{2}sinx$

i.e.~$sinx = 0, \dfrac{1}{2} = sinx + cosx$

$x = \pi$

or~$\dfrac{1}{2} = sin \left(x + $\dfrac{π}{4}\right)

$⇒ $sin\dfrac{π}{6} =$sin \left($x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)$

$x + \dfrac{π}{4} = \pi - \dfrac{π}{6},$2\pi + $\dfrac{π}{6}$

$x = \dfrac{5\pi}{6} - \dfrac{π}{4},x = \dfrac{13\pi}{6} - \dfrac{π}{4}$

$x = \dfrac{7\pi}{12},x = \dfrac{23\pi}{12}$

Hence sum of abscissas of all the points of intersection

$= $\pi + $\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{23\pi}{12}$

$= \dfrac{12\pi + 7\pi + 23}{12} = \dfrac{42\pi}{12}$

$\dfrac{k\pi}{12} = \dfrac{42\pi}{12}⇒ k = 42$

$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential~equation $xdy - ydx = \sqrt{\left(x^{2} - y^{2}\right)}dx, x \ge 1$, with~$y ( 1 ) = 0$. If the area bounded by the line $x = 1, x = e^{π}, y = 0$~and $y = y ( x )$ is $\alphae^{2\pi} + \beta,$~then the value of $10 ( \alpha + \beta )$ is equal to ___ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $xdy - ydx = \sqrt{x^{2} - y^{2}}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{xdy - ydx}{x2} = \dfrac{1}{x}\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{y2}{x2}}dx$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{d\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}{1 - \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)2} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = ln\left|x\right| + c$

at $x = 1, y = 0 ⇒ c = 0$

$y = xsin ( lnx )$

$A = {∫}_{1}^{e\pi}xsin\left(lnx\right)dx$

$x = e^{t}, dx = e^{t}dt ⇒ {∫}_{0}^{π}e^{2t}sin\left(t\right)dt = A$

$\alphae^{2\pi} + \beta = {\dfrac{e2t}{5} ( 2sint - cost )}_{0}^{π} = \dfrac{1 + e^{2\pi}}{5}$

$\alpha = \dfrac{1}{5}, \beta = \dfrac{1}{5}$

So,~$10 ( \alpha + \beta ) = 4$

questions.q: If the solution curve, of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y - 2}{x - y}$ passing through the point $( 2, 1 )$ is $\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y - 1}{x - 1}\right) - \dfrac{1}{β}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\alpha + \left(\dfrac{y - 1}{x - 1}\right)2\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left|x - 1\right|$, then $5\beta + \alpha$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y - 2}{x - y}$

Now, finding the intersection point of $x + y - 2 = 0$ and $x - y = 0$.

$⇒ x + x - 2 = 0, x = y$

$⇒ x = 1, y = 1$

$⇒ \left(x, y\right) ≡ \left($1, 1\right)$

Let, $x = X + 1, y = Y + 1$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dY}{dX} = \dfrac{X + Y}{X - Y}

Putting, $Y = tX$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dY}{dX} =$t + $X\dfrac{dt}{dX}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1 + t}{1 - t} =$t + $X\dfrac{dt}{dX}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1 + t - t + t^{2}}{1 - t} ===X\dfrac{dt}{dX}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{X}$dX = $\dfrac{1 - t}{1 + t^{2}}$dt$

$⇒ ∫ $\dfrac{1}{X}$dX = ∫ $\dfrac{1 - t}{1 + t^{2}}$dt$

$⇒ log\left|X\right| = \tan^{- 1}t - $\d$dfrac{1}{2}log\left|$1 + t^{2}\right| + C$

$⇒ $log\left|$x - 1\right| = \tan^{- $1} \left(\dfrac{y - 1}{x - 1}\right) - \dddfrac{1}{2}$log\left|1 + \$left(\dfrac{y - 1}{x - 1}\right)$2\right| + C$

It is given that the solution curve passes through \left(2, 1\right)$.

$⇒ log\left|2 - 1\right| = \tan^{- $1} $\$left(\dfrac{1 - 1}{2 - 1}\right) - \ddfrac{1}{2}$log \left|1 + \$left(\dfrac{1 - 1}{2 - 1}\right)$2\right| + C$

$⇒ 0 = \tan^{- 1}\left(0\right) - $\d$dfrac{1}{2}log\left|$1\right| + C$

$⇒ C = 0$

$⇒ $\alpha =$1, $\beta =$2$

$⇒ $5\beta + \alpha =$11$.

$

questions.q: Let the solution curve $x = x ( y ) , 0 < y < \dfrac{π}{2}$, of the differential equation \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(cosy\right)\right)2cosydx - \left(1 + 3x\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(cosy\right)\right)sinydy = 0$ satisfy $x\left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2\log_{\mathrm{e}}2}$. If $x\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\log_{\mathrm{e}}m - \log_{\mathrm{e}}n}$, where~$m$~and $n$ are coprime, then $mn$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(cosy\right)\right)2cosydx - \left(1 + 3x\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(cosy\right)\right)sinydy = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} + \left(\dfrac{- 3tany}{lncosy}\right)x = \dfrac{siny}{\left(In cosy\right)2 \cdot cosy}$

Which is a linear differential equation,

So, Integrating factor will be,~$IF = e^{3 ∫ \dfrac{- tany}{lncosy}dy} = \left(lncosy\right)3$

So, solution of differential equation is given by,
$x\left(lncosy\right)3 = ∫ \dfrac{siny}{cosy}\left(lncosy\right)dy$
$⇒ x\left(lncosy\right)3 = \dfrac{- \left(lncosy\right)2}{2} + c$

Now using the given value of~$x\left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2ln2}$
We get,~$c = 0$
Hence,~$x = \dfrac{- 1}{2lncosy}$

Now finding,~$x\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) = - \dfrac{1}{2ln\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{ln4 - ln3}$

Now on comparing with~$\dfrac{1}{\log_{\mathrm{e}}m - \log_{\mathrm{e}}n}$~we get,~$m = 4, n = 3$

Hence,~$mn = 12$

$
